Plain text matches any part of a value, and ignores case. Write /^ab/i for a regular expression, or score > 5 to test one column. A test on one column skips every row group whose statistics exclude a match.

The viewer reads the footer of each file first, which holds the schema, the row count and the statistics of every column. That is a few kilobytes, so a folder of shards opens in about the time it takes to list it.

A page of rows is read on demand, and only for the columns on show. Parquet keeps its rows in groups, so the reader takes the pages it needs from the group that holds the row you asked for, and leaves the rest of the file alone. Each file is read in parts, and your files stay in this browser tab.

Open one .parquet file, or a folder of shards that the viewer reads as one dataset. It reads the footer of each file first, and a page of rows only when you ask for it. Your files stay in this browser tab.
